title: Constant Contact Pricing Explained (2026): All Plans
summary: Constant Contact pricing ranges from Lite for simple campaigns to Premium for advanced controls. Pick the tier that fits your email list size.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Does Constant Contact have a free plan?


Budget for a paid tier from the day you commit, because Constant Contact has a free trial rather than a permanent free plan.


The trial is useful for testing your list import and one real send, but it's not a place to run a list long term.


Check the current trial terms on Constant Contact's pricing page before you sign up, because the length and limits are the vendor's to change.


### Can I cancel Constant Contact and get a refund?


You can cancel at any time, but refund eligibility depends on the terms attached to your billing period, so don't assume a prorated return.


Treat the cancellation date as the cost control: cancel before a renewal, not after it. If you're on a prepaid term, read the refund language in your account's terms before paying, since that's where an unused month or year is either returned or lost.


### Does Constant Contact charge more when I exceed my contact limit?


Yes, going past your tier's contact count moves you into a higher-priced band, and the bill follows the list rather than your sending habits. That's the jump this article keeps pointing at.


A list you stopped mailing may keep pushing you upward, because unsubscribed and bounced contacts can still count toward your total until they're removed. Clean it before a renewal and the next band may never apply.


### Is Constant Contact cheaper if I pay annually?


Pay for a longer term up front and the effective monthly rate generally drops compared with paying month to month. What you give up is flexibility: you commit cash up front, so an unexpected list change or a plan you outgrow costs more to correct.


If your contact count is stable and your plan fits, the discount is worth taking. If your list is still moving, stay monthly until it settles.


### Can I downgrade from Premium to Standard?


Yes, you can move to a lower plan, but the move is only as clean as the features you stop using. Anything you built on Premium-only tools, such as advanced automation or segmentation, may stop working or become unavailable on Standard.


Audit what you actually rely on first. If nothing breaks, the downgrade lowers the bill. If something does, you've found the feature that was forcing the upgrade all along.
